question: What is the difference between a CPU and a GPU architecturally?
answer: A CPU has a few powerful cores (4-64) optimized for low-latency sequential tasks, with large caches, out-of-order execution, and branch prediction. A GPU has thousands of smaller, simpler cores optimized for high-throughput parallel tasks. GPUs have high memory bandwidth but higher latency per operation. CPUs excel at control-heavy, branchy, sequential code. GPUs excel at data-parallel workloads where the same operation runs on thousands of data points simultaneously.
